market_name: Ukraine signs peace deal with Russia before 2027?

trade_eligibility.reason: Below minimum expected move or unclear direction.

time_plan.30m: Check whether the probability move is backed by any wire headline (Reuters/Bloomberg on talks, Witkoff/Zelensky/Putin statements) or is pure market noise; note Rheinmetall pre/after-hours quote and sector peers (Leonardo, BAE, Thales).
time_plan.1h: Confirm move persists in the prediction market and whether defense ETFs (ITA/EUAD) and peers are moving in sympathy; distinguish idiosyncratic from thematic.
time_plan.2h: Re-assess against European equity index behavior and gas prices to validate a coherent de-escalation narrative rather than a one-name blip.
time_plan.6h: Check for official denials/confirmations; defense names often retrace quickly if 'peace talk' headlines are walked back. Reduce conviction if no corroboration.
time_plan.12h: Mark realized move vs the -550bps expectation; log whether the prediction-market move led, lagged, or was unrelated to defense-equity price action.

predictions.reasoning: European defense primes like Rheinmetall have re-rated massively on sustained Russia-Ukraine conflict and expectations of persistent elevated European defense spending. A sharp upward move in the implied probability of a Ukraine-Russia peace/ceasefire instrument would compress that war premium, as markets price lower near-term escalation and a possible plateau in the fastest phase of rearmament. Rheinmetall is the single most war-sensitive liquid European name, so it is the cleanest directional proxy for a de-escalation signal.

predictions.asset: European natural gas / energy risk premium
predictions.tradable_instrument_name: Dutch TTF natural gas futures (European benchmark)

trade_eligibility.reason: Below minimum expected move or unclear direction.

time_plan.30m: Verify any genuine news catalyst; check TTF front-month and Brent reaction, plus EUR/USD for a broader risk-on read.
time_plan.1h: See if energy move is consistent with the defense-equity signal (coherent de-escalation theme) or divergent.
time_plan.2h: Assess whether storage/weather/LNG headlines are dominating energy instead of geopolitics, which would void the thesis.
time_plan.6h: Re-check for sanctions-relief commentary; absent concrete flow implications, fade the energy signal.
time_plan.12h: Record realized TTF/Brent move vs expectation and whether geopolitics or fundamentals explained it.

predictions.reasoning: A credible peace/ceasefire path would reduce the geopolitical risk premium in European energy and raise the possibility of eventual normalization of Russian gas/energy flows, pressuring European gas prices lower and modestly easing crude. However, the link is indirect and slow: sanctions relief and pipeline restarts would lag any signature by months, and current European gas is driven more by LNG/weather/storage than by Russian flow expectations. This is a weak, low-conviction mapping.

evidence_used: Market question: probability Ukraine signs a written peace/ceasefire instrument with Russia before end-2026
Broad resolution criteria (any signed framework/roadmap with ceasefire or defined peace process qualifies; only Ukraine's signature needed)
Known sensitivity of European defense primes (Rheinmetall, Leonardo, Thales, BAE) to the war premium
European energy complex's historical sensitivity to Russia-Ukraine geopolitical risk
uncertainty_notes: A move in implied probability is not the signing itself; 12h asset moves from a probability shift alone are usually modest and may not reach the 700bps tradable threshold.
Defense re-rating also reflects structural NATO spending commitments that would persist even after a ceasefire, muting the downside.
Energy prices are currently dominated by LNG supply, storage, and weather, weakening the Russia-flow linkage.
Russian assets (the most direct beneficiaries) are largely untradable/sanctioned, forcing reliance on second-order proxies.

llm_justification.summary: A sharp rise in the implied probability of a Ukraine-Russia peace/ceasefire instrument should compress the war risk premium: most cleanly in European defense equities (Rheinmetall as the most war-sensitive liquid proxy, directionally down) and, more weakly and slowly, in European natural gas/energy prices (down on reduced geopolitical premium and eventual normalization hopes). Both mappings are directionally plausible but face significant dilution—structural defense spending and non-geopolitical energy drivers—so conviction is moderate-to-low and 12h magnitudes may fall short of the tradable threshold absent an actual signing headline.
key_assumptions: The probability move reflects genuine de-escalation information, not noise or a resolution-criteria technicality.
Defense primes still carry a meaningful war premium that can decompress on peace signals.
Markets interpret a Ukrainian signature as reducing, not increasing, regional conflict risk.
failure_modes: The move is already public (peace talks widely reported), so assets have already repriced and there is no leak edge.
Defense stocks hold up because investors view elevated European rearmament as structural and sticky regardless of a ceasefire.
A ceasefire signing could paradoxically be read as temporary/unstable, keeping risk premia elevated (direction unclear/reverses).
Energy proxy is weakly exposed—LNG/weather/storage dominate, so gas fails to respond.
The prediction-market move reverses quickly as a 'peace' headline is denied or walked back, whipsawing proxies.
llm_justification.why_not_ex_post: The card is timestamped, content-hashed, and never overwritten. Execution must reject any card created after an anomaly's trigger time.
